messages:
Samira (Design): Quick follow-up from the model-catalog critique. Three UX pain points today: saved views are invisible in the drawer, performance badges are stealing visual weight from model titles, and pinning semantics are unclear (model vs version). I sketched a couple low-risk tweaks below.

Ethan (PM): +1 on all. Saved views (what we call presets elsewhere) need discoverability. Idea: replace the top of the filter drawer with a compact chip row showing the top 4 saved views, then a "More" chevron to open the full manager. That keeps height low and makes them discoverable.

Rohit (Backend): Sounds fine. For persistence we'll add a small user_prefs entry for saved_view_id and pinned_versions. API endpoints: GET /v1/me/prefs and POST /v1/me/prefs. We'll document contract for migration from localStorage.

Noah (Frontend): Visual hierarchy for badges: currently full pill with shadow. Proposal: convert to ghost-style chips (no heavy bg), reduce font to 11px, move to the far right column so names don't wrap prematurely. Example: `.perf-chip{ background:transparent; border:1px solid rgba(7,10,15,0.06); color:var(--muted); font-size:11px; padding:2px 6px; border-radius:6px; }` Also add a compact density toggle to switch between numeric & icon-only badge modes.

Lina (A11y): Accessibility: chips must meet contrast and be keyboard focusable. Use roving tabindex for the saved-view chips so arrow keys navigate them and screen readers announce state: `role=\"toolbar\"` and each chip `role=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"false\"`. Badges need `aria-label` with context: e.g., `aria-label=\"98th percentile latency: 220 milliseconds\"`. If we implement icon-only mode, ensure tooltip text and aria-label remain available.

Samira (Design): On pin semantics: two options: pin per-model (keeps last chosen version when opening model page) or pin per-version (locks compare to a single version). I prefer pin-by-version for reproducibility. Microcopy: pin button tooltip "Pin this version to your account". If we later add team-level pins, we can add a scope dropdown.

Ethan (PM): For MVP pick pin-by-version (user-scoped). Track analytics `catalog.pin` with props { scope: "user", model_id, version, source: "compare" }. Also track `catalog.view_selected` when a saved view is applied.

Rohit (Backend): We'll store pinned_versions as [{model_id, version, pinned_at}] and exclude retired versions by soft-delete. Edge case: pinned version missing in an incoming compare selection -> do not auto-select; show a non-blocking banner: "Pinned version not included in this compare."

qa-bot: qa-bot: New build for feature branch `ux/catalog-savedviews-chips` deployed to staging: https://staging.redwood.ai/catalog/compare (staging). Run smoke tests.

Noah (Frontend): Checklist for the PR: 1) add compact saved-view chips row with roving keyboard nav, 2) implement ghost-style perf chips and right-align them, 3) add small density toggle (number / icon), 4) pin button persists to API, 5) add aria-labels & focus styles. I'll include screenshots and keyboard walkthrough.

Lina (A11y): I'll validate NVDA and VoiceOver flows on staging. Note: ensure chip focus order is logical (filters follow chips). Also confirm tooltip text is announced on long-press for touch.

Samira (Design): Microcopy suggestions: chips label "Saved views" above the row, "More views" for chevron, pin tooltip "Pin version 1saves this selection to your account2" (edit: actual tooltip: "Pin version 0saves this selection to your account10"), and banner "Pinned version not included in this compare." I'll tidy copy in a short spec and attach to the Jira.

Ethan (PM): I'll open the ticket with acceptance criteria (chips visible, badge de-emphasis, density toggle, pin persistence API, analytics, A11y checklist). Tentative ship target: next sprint.

Samira (Design): Thanks everyone. Once Noah's PR lands, I'll update the prototype and paste the staging link in the Jira for review.
